hypotheses.justification: The proof passes this hypothesis on to `Chart.clifford` (RiemannRochTheorem/Corollaries.lean, line 500). There it is the unused binder `_hdeg₀`: `Chart.clifford` is just `clifford_of_ell_pos k K hW D hℓD hℓW`. `Chart.clifford_of_ell_pos` (line 487) needs only `IsCanonical`, `0 < ell D` and `0 < ell (W - D)`. Its docstring says the bounds `0 ≤ deg D ≤ 2g − 2` are not required. So the intrinsic proof can be rewritten without `hdeg₀` and `hdeg₀'`: keep `hW'` and the `ell_eq_chart` rewrites, then use `simpa using Chart.clifford_of_ell_pos k K hW' ((divisorEquivChart k K).symm D) hℓD hℓW`. The `simpa` step that turns the chart degree into `D.deg` (`Divisor.chart_deg`) is the same one the current proof already uses. Mathematically this is expected anyway: `ℓ(D) > 0` makes `D` linearly equivalent to an effective divisor, so `deg D ≥ 0`. This hypothesis and `hdeg₁` can be deleted on their own or together.

The same reasoning applies. In `Chart.clifford` the matching binder `_hdeg₁` is never used, because the inequality follows from `Chart.clifford_of_ell_pos k K hW D hℓD hℓW`. That lemma combines `ell_add_ell_le`, `ell_canonical` and `riemann_roch` and makes no degree assumption. The intrinsic theorem can call `Chart.clifford_of_ell_pos` on `(divisorEquivChart k K).symm D` and drop `hdeg₁'`; the remaining `simpa` translation of degree and genus is unchanged. Mathematically, `ℓ(W − D) > 0` already gives `deg(W − D) ≥ 0`, so `deg D ≤ 2g − 2`. This hypothesis can be removed together with `hdeg₀`.
